restDayGuidance: Monday and Thursday is an original separated-day calendar example, not an NHS-tested recovery interval.

trigger: All listed movements remain controlled and manageable; do not infer a personal readiness score.
action: Build gradually over weeks as the NHS describes. Retain controlled practice and seek qualified instruction when choosing load; no fixed weekly increment is supplied.
ceiling: Do not force the repetitions, accept loss of the linked movement control or automatically add a third set or heavier load.
floor: Begin with manageable practice rather than forcing two complete sets. Reduce the attempted work or pause when control cannot be maintained; seek instruction if the published version is unsuitable.
stallResponse: Retain or reduce attempted work and obtain appropriate instruction; no automatic load adjustment or pain diagnosis.

matchingRules: Both published guides describe a press; this is an original option, not proof of equivalent load, muscle activation or outcome.
Use only the exact published version already learned and appropriate to your available equipment and abilities.
disallowedChanges: Do not transfer a dumbbell load to a bodyweight movement, silently alter the prescription or treat a substitution as medical advice.
Do not infer equivalence or automatic suitability from shared movement classification.

scienceRationale.decision: Organize 2 static source-scoped practice sessions; day placement and exercise combination are original authorship.
qualifiers: The linked science articles distinguish training variables and gradual progression; they do not test this whole program.
The NHS framework supplies the general set/repetition context; no superiority, individualized effort or duration claim is inferred.

measurementGuidance.howToUse: Track completed sessions only if you choose local tracking; missing sessions are not automatically failures.
limitations: Completion does not prove adaptation, safety, readiness or suitability.

generalBoundaries: Read the exact linked technique instructions and the NHS safety information before exercising.

stopSignals: The NHS advises stopping immediately if pain occurs or you become unwell; seek appropriate help for symptoms that persist or cause concern.

contentStatusNote: Source-verified and machine-validated personal-use publication; original arrangement, no independent human or clinical review or NHS endorsement.
summary: An original 3-day general strength-practice arrangement for adults who have already learned these intermediate techniques. It uses the NHS general strength framework and links exact published movement versions; the complete arrangement has not been tested as a program.

designedToSupport: Organizing source-scoped strength practice using an authored static calendar.
doesNotGuarantee: Specific strength, hypertrophy, injury-prevention or rehabilitation outcomes.

notDesignedFor: Diagnosis, rehabilitation, athletic peaking or individual medical clearance.

bestFor: Adults in good health with reasonable fitness and prior instruction in every listed movement.
notFor: An untrained novice or anyone unsure about suitability, with pain, illness, injury or a recent health event requiring professional advice.
prerequisites: Prior instruction and comfortable control of goblet squats, Romanian deadlifts, bench-supported rows, bench presses and bird-dog movements; the linked ACE guides include intermediate techniques.
A stable exercise bench, clear floor space and manageable dumbbells.
